mainTopic: יבום after-born brothers, and the משנה on which forbidden יבמות do חליצה but not יבום
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to the רבנן, who learn from ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ that a brother born after יבום is still forbidden to the יבמה. The גמרא explains that ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ makes her fully a wife to the brother who did יבום, while ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ keeps her forbidden to a later brother: leniency goes with the permitted case, prohibition with the forbidden case. It then defends רבי שמעון's view against a challenge from a half-sister case: a brother's-wife prohibition can be lifted through יבום, but a sister is never permitted. A new משנה follows. An ערוה needs neither חליצה nor יבום. A woman under an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה does חליצה but not יבום, and the sister of an ערוה is a normal יבמה. The גמרא explains the word כלל (two versions of רפרם about the צרת אילונית), whose sister the משנה means, and why each prohibition gets its name, including רבי יהודה's reversed labels and רבא's 'קדש עצמך במותר לך'. Finally, it asks why a widow from אירוסין cannot do יבום with a כהן גדול. רב גידל learns from ״יבמתו״ that women forbidden by a לאו do חליצה only, and a rule from another פסוק leaves out חייבי כריתות. The amud ends by asking why ״יבמתו״ goes with לאוין rather than כריתות, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: If the first יבום bond remains, divorce should also need חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching on the משנה: a man who did יבום may divorce his יבמה with a גט and may remarry her. It then asks: by the logic of ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״, the first יבום bond should still be on her, so she should need חליצה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...that he divorces her with a גט and may take her back. There too, let us say ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״: the first יבום bond is still upon her, so she should need חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the רבנן's reading of ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״. If the יבום bond stays on her after the marriage, then a simple גט should not be enough to end it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ teaches that even after יבום she is still 'the יבמה' as far as a later-born brother is concerned. If that is true, the old bond never fully goes away. Then the הלכה that a גט alone is enough, with no חליצה, looks contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall perform יבום with her' (דברים 25:5)
The original יבום bond tying her to the brothers
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from the יבום bond

phrases.english: that he divorces her with a get, and may take her back.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching on a משנה quoted at the end of the previous page: once he marries his יבמה she is like his wife in every way, so a גט alone ends it and he may remarry her.

phrases.english: There too, let us say: "and perform yibum with her"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: the first yibum bond is still upon her,
so she should require chalitza!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun on the previous page against the רבנן's reading of ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's reading that ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ keeps the first יבום bond on her even after the marriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bond remains, divorcing her with only a גט should not be enough. She should also need חליצה, yet the משנה says a גט alone works.

steps.title: Once he takes her, she is fully his wife
steps.stepSummary: The verse ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ teaches that after יבום she becomes his wife in every respect, so a גט alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״. Once he has taken her, she becomes like his wife in every way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a different phrase from the same פסוק. That phrase shows that after יבום she is completely his wife, so a regular גט ends the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ alone might suggest the old bond lingers. ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ shows that for the man who did יבום, she becomes a normal wife. A normal wife needs only a גט, not חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And take her to him as a wife' (דברים 25:5)
Like his wife in every respect

phrases.english: It is different there
for the verse says: "and take her to him as a wife,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: once he has taken her
she becomes like his wife in every respect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by bringing a different phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ keeps the bond on her, divorce should require חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ makes her fully his wife, so a גט is enough.

steps.title: Then the later-born brother should also be permitted
steps.stepSummary: If she becomes fully his wife, then the brother born after the יבום should also be allowed to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, here too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer back on itself. If ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ makes her a full wife, the later-born brother case should also be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'fully his wife' should erase the old יבום status completely. Then a brother born afterward should not see her as his dead brother's wife who is forbidden to him. This would contradict the רבנן's ruling.

phrases.english: If so, here too!
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the brother born after the יבום: by this logic, he should also be allowed to marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by applying it to the later-born brother case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ to say she is fully his wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is fully his wife, the old יבום status is gone, so the later-born brother should be permitted, against the רבנן.

steps.title: The word ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ keeps her forbidden to the later brother
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״, and that word teaches that for a later-born brother she is still considered the יבמה, so she stays forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רחמנא wrote ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ is still there to teach something. Its job is to keep her forbidden to the brother born later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each phrase has its own job. ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ handles divorce, so no חליצה is needed. ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ handles the later-born brother, so she stays forbidden to him.

phrases.english: But the Merciful One wrote: "and perform yibum with her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each phrase of the פסוק is given a separate job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she is fully his wife, the later brother should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ specifically keeps the old יבום status for the later-born brother, so she stays forbidden to him.

steps.title: Why assign each verse this way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason there is to apply ״וּלְקָחָהּ״ to divorce and ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ to the later brother, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the split made in step 4. It asks why we assigned the two phrases this way and not the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swapping them is also possible. Then she would need חליצה after divorce, and the later brother would be permitted. The גמרא wants a reason for choosing the first arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And what did you see?' — what is your reason for this choice?

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why use each verse for the case you picked, and not switch them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way the two phrases were divided in steps 2 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of ״וּלְקָחָהּ״ to divorce and ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ to the later-born brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reverse assignment seems just as possible, so the choice needs a reason.

steps.title: Leniency goes with leniency, prohibition with prohibition
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense to apply the permitting verse to the permitted case, the man who did יבום. The forbidding verse goes with the forbidden case, the later-born brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable to toss the leniency onto the leniency, and the prohibition onto the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a logical reason for the split. The verse that makes her a full wife fits the brother who already married her. The verse that keeps the old bond fits the brother who is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who did יבום was allowed to marry her, so it fits to make that permission complete. The brother born later falls under the prohibition of a brother's wife, so it fits to keep the prohibition strong for him. Matching like with like is the most sensible reading.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, ״וּלְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה״ makes her a full wife to the brother who did יבום, so a גט alone is enough. ״וְיִבְּמָהּ״ keeps her forbidden to a brother born afterward. The logic is: leniency goes with the permitted case, and prohibition goes with the forbidden case.

phrases.english: It stands to reason: toss the permitted onto the permitted,
and toss the prohibited onto the prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and closes the discussion of the רבנן's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrases could be assigned in reverse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting phrase belongs with the permitted case and the forbidding phrase with the forbidden case.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי שמעון from a half-sister case
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון permits a later-born brother because he 'found her permitted'. The גמרא challenges this with a case: a man's maternal half-sister married his paternal half-brother, then he was born, then the husband died. By the same logic, she should be allowed to him in יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון, who said 'since he came and found her in a permitted state, and she was never forbidden to him even for one moment': if so, take his maternal half-sister who married his paternal half-brother. Afterward this brother was born, and then the husband died. She should do יבום with him, since he came and found her in a permitted state!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to רבי שמעון's opinion and attacks his reasoning. It gives a case where his reasoning would permit something clearly forbidden: marrying his own sister. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says the later-born brother may do יבום because when he was born she was already a permitted, married woman. In the half-sister case, she too was already permitted, married to a brother who was not related to her. Yet she is this baby's sister, a full ערוה, so his reasoning seems to lead to an impossible result.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he came into the world and found her in a permitted state
But if so (introduces a result that cannot be right)
His sister from his mother (maternal half-sister)
His brother from his father (paternal half-brother)

steps.confusionAlert: The husband and wife here are not related: he is the newborn's brother through the father, and she is the newborn's sister through the mother. Their marriage was fully allowed. The problem is only between her and the newborn.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who said:
since he came and found her in a permitted state

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָמְדָה עָלָיו שָׁעָה אַחַת בְּאִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: and she never stood forbidden to him even for one moment,
but if so,
his sister from his mother
whom his brother from his father married,
and afterward the brother was born, and the husband died
she should do yibum with him,
since he came and found her in a permitted state!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבנן's view to challenge רבי שמעון's reasoning about a later-born brother.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reasoning: 'since he came and found her in a permitted state'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning would allow a man to do יבום with his own maternal half-sister, which is clearly forbidden as an ערוה.

steps.title: A sister's prohibition does not disappear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge from step 7. In that case the widow is the later-born brother's own sister, and that prohibition does not simply vanish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition of his sister, where did it go?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. Even if she was 'found permitted' as a brother's wife, she is still his sister, and that prohibition is still there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7's case the woman is the later-born brother's maternal half-sister. רבי שמעון's idea of 'finding her permitted' only removes the problem of a brother's wife. It cannot remove the separate prohibition of a sister, which stays in full force.

keyTerms.meaning: Where did it go? (meaning: it couldn't have just disappeared)

phrases.english: The prohibition of his sister, where did it go?!
phrases.notes: In step 7's case, the widow is his half-sister through their mother, so she is forbidden to him as a sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a second, separate prohibition that רבי שמעון's logic does not touch
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she was 'found permitted', she should be allowed to the later-born brother even though she is his sister
steps.terutzMaskana: The sister prohibition remains, so she is forbidden to him

steps.title: Then the brother's-wife prohibition should not disappear either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same argument around. The prohibition of the wife of a brother he never lived alongside was also already there, so why should it disappear for רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: the prohibition of a brother who was not in the world with him, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If a prohibition cannot just 'go away', then the brother's-wife prohibition should not go away either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's case, the woman was first married to a brother who lived before the later brother was born. That already made her forbidden as the wife of a brother 'not in his world'. If a sister's prohibition stays, why does this one disappear?

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same logic applies
A brother who was not alive at the same time as him
A brother's wife (forbidden except through יבום)

phrases.english: Here too:
the prohibition of a brother who was not in the world [with him]
phrases.notes: He means the first husband, who died before the later brother was born. A wife of such a brother never falls to him for יבום.

phrases.english: where did it go?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי אִיסּוּר אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּעוֹלָם לְהֵיכָן אֲזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of step 8 against רבי שמעון's own ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that the later-born brother finds her permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a prohibition that already existed cannot vanish, then the brother's-wife prohibition from the first brother should not vanish either

steps.title: A prohibition that can be permitted is different
steps.stepSummary: The sister prohibition never has a permitted form. The brother's-wife prohibition does have one, through יבום, so it can be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This prohibition [of a sister] has no permission. That prohibition [of a brother's wife] has a permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains why a brother's-wife prohibition can disappear while a sister's prohibition cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sister is never permitted under any circumstances, so her prohibition never goes away. A brother's wife can become permitted through יבום. Once the second brother did יבום, the old prohibition was lifted before the third brother was born, so he 'found her permitted'.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, only a prohibition that has a permitted form, like a brother's wife through יבום, can be removed. A sister is never permitted, so her prohibition stays.

phrases.english: This prohibition has no permission,
phrases.notes: This is the sister prohibition. A sister is never allowed.

phrases.english: that prohibition has a permission.
phrases.notes: This is the brother's-wife prohibition, which יבום can lift.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אִיסּוּרָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ הֶיתֵּירָא הַאי אִיסּוּרָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֶיתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by drawing a distinction between the two prohibitions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both prohibitions should behave the same way
steps.terutzMaskana: A prohibition that can become permitted can be removed. One that is never permitted cannot.

steps.title: משנה: the rule for forbidden יבמות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה states a general rule. An ערוה does neither חליצה nor יבום. A woman under an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: They stated a principle about a יבמה. Any woman who is forbidden as an ערוה neither does חליצה nor יבום. A woman under a מצוה prohibition or a holiness prohibition does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the basic rule for a יבמה who is forbidden to the יבם, sorted by the type of prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערוה prohibition removes the יבום connection completely, so she needs nothing at all. The weaker prohibitions do not remove the connection, so she still needs חליצה. But she cannot do יבום, because she is forbidden to him.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two results. An ערוה is completely exempt and needs no חליצה. The other prohibitions still need חליצה, even though יבום is not allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: They stated a principle about a yevama:
any woman who is forbidden as an ervah
does not do ḥalitza and does not do yibbum.
A מצוה prohibition and a holiness prohibition:
phrases.notes: The משנה explains these two terms itself, right at the end (step 13).

phrases.english: she does ḥalitza but does not do yibbum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערוה: neither חליצה nor יבום. איסור מצוה or איסור קדושה: חליצה, not יבום.

steps.title: The sister of the forbidden woman is still available
steps.stepSummary: When one sister is an ערוה to the יבם, the other sister, her sister-in-law, may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her sister who is her יבמה does חליצה or does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule. One sister being an ערוה does not block the other sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two sisters falling to one יבם block each other. Here one sister is an ערוה, so she never really fell to him at all. That leaves her sister as a regular יבמה, with both options open.

phrases.english: Her sister, who is her yevama,
phrases.notes: The case is two sisters married to two brothers who died. One sister is an ערוה to the remaining brother, so 'her sister' here means the other one.

phrases.english: does ḥalitza or does yibbum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule within the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sister of a woman who is an ערוה to the יבם may do חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: Defining מצוה and holiness prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its terms. An איסור מצוה means the rabbinic שניות. An איסור קדושה means marriages forbidden by the rules of כהונה or of lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה prohibition: secondary relatives, forbidden by the words of the Sages. A holiness prohibition: a widow to a כהן גדול; a divorcee or a חלוצה to a regular כהן; a ממזרת or a נתינה to a Jew; and a Jewish woman to a נתין or a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the two terms it used in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור מצוה refers to relatives the חכמים forbade, called שניות. An איסור קדושה covers marriages forbidden because of כהונה or because of lineage. In all of these cases the woman does חליצה but not יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A daughter born from a forbidden union
A woman descended from the גבעונים

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. An ערוה needs nothing at all. An איסור מצוה (שניות) or an איסור קדושה (כהונה or lineage) needs חליצה but cannot do יבום. When one sister is an ערוה, the other sister is a normal יבמה.

phrases.english: A מצוה prohibition means secondary relatives, forbidden by the words of the Sages.
A holiness prohibition means a widow to a High Priest,
a divorcee or a woman who did ḥalitza to a regular priest,
a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman to an Israelite,
and an Israelite woman to a Gibeonite man or a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the terms used in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An איסור מצוה means the rabbinic שניות. An איסור קדושה means marriages forbidden by כהונה or lineage.

steps.title: What does the word 'rule' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's word כלל ('a general rule') is meant to add.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה says 'a rule.' What does that come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by asking a question. It wants to know what the word 'כלל' adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה says 'this is the rule,' the גמרא assumes it is hinting at a case that is not spelled out. All the ערוה cases were already listed in the first פרק, so the word must be adding something new.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule; a word that usually hints at extra cases
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The word 'rule': what does it come to include?
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה's opening words in step 11, which are phrased as a general rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה quoted in steps 11-13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the extra word כלל adds.

steps.title: רפרם: it includes the rival wife of an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא says the word כלל adds the צרה of an אילונית, following רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said: It comes to include the rival wife of an אילונית, in line with רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם בר פפא answers the question. The word כלל teaches that the צרה of an אילונית is also exempt from חליצה and יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אילונית is a woman who cannot have children, so she herself does not do יבום. רב אסי holds that her צרה is also exempt, because she is the צרה of a woman who stays forbidden to the יבם. The word כלל brings this case into the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The co-wife of a woman who cannot have children
An אמורא who holds that the צרה of an אילונית is exempt

phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said:
It comes to include the rival wife of an aylonit,
and this follows Rav Asi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא: לְאֵתוֹיֵי צָרַת אַיְלוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלל includes the צרת אילונית, who is exempt following רב אסי.

steps.title: Second version: what does 'forbidden as ערוה' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: A second version reads an inference from the משנה: only the צרה of an ערוה is forbidden, so what case is being left out?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it differently: 'Anyone whose prohibition is an ערוה prohibition' means only then is her rival wife forbidden. So if her prohibition is not an ערוה prohibition, her rival wife is not forbidden. What does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of רפרם's teaching that is attached to a different line. It draws an inference from the משנה's wording and asks what that inference leaves out. This sets up רפרם's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the focus is on the words 'forbidden as ערוה.' They suggest that a woman forbidden for any other reason does not make her צרה forbidden. The question is which real case this limit is aimed at.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: a second version of the teaching
What does it come to exclude?

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
'Anyone whose prohibition is a prohibition of ערוה':
it is only then that her rival wife is forbidden,
but if her prohibition is not a prohibition of ערוה,
her rival wife is not forbidden.
What does this come to exclude?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: כׇּל שֶׁאִיסּוּרָהּ אִיסּוּר עֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version that attaches רפרם's teaching to a different line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is excluded by the limit 'only an ערוה makes her צרה forbidden.'

steps.title: רפרם: it excludes the rival wife of an אילונית
steps.stepSummary: In this version רפרם says the limit excludes the צרת אילונית, which goes against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: It excludes the rival wife of an אילונית, and this is not like רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם answers that the case left out is the צרה of an אילונית. She is not exempt, so she does חליצה or יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of the first version. Here the אילונית is not treated as an ערוה, so her צרה stays bound to the יבם. That means this version argues with רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And not in line with רב אסי

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of רפרם reach opposite results. In the first, the צרת אילונית is exempt, like רב אסי. In the second, she is not exempt, against רב אסי.
steps.confusionAlert: Both versions are by the same רפרם and talk about the same צרת אילונית, but they reach opposite results. Don't blend them together.

phrases.english: Rafram said:
It excludes the rival wife of an aylonit,
and this is not like Rav Asi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16, with the opposite result from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limit excludes the צרת אילונית, who is not exempt, against רב אסי.

steps.title: Whose sister does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'her sister who is her יבמה' and asks whose sister this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Her sister who is her יבמה.' Whose sister is it talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks a clarifying question. It sets up the two possible readings that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the sister may do חליצה or יבום, but it did not say which forbidden woman she is the sister of. It could be the sister of a woman under an איסור מצוה, or the sister of an ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her sister who is her sister-in-law (also waiting for יבום)

phrases.english: 'Her sister who is her yevama.'
Whose sister?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'her sister' means the sister of an איסור מצוה woman or of an ערוה.

steps.title: It can't be the sister of an איסור מצוה woman
steps.stepSummary: If it were the sister of a woman under an איסור מצוה, she would be the sister of his זקוקה, and that case has different rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the sister of a woman under an איסור מצוה, there is a problem. By Torah law that woman is fully waiting before him for יבום. So he would be meeting the sister of a woman bound to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור מצוה is only rabbinic, so by Torah law that woman is truly bound to the יבם. Her sister would then be the 'sister of his זקוקה,' a case already taught elsewhere with its own rules. So the משנה's simple 'she does חליצה or יבום' cannot be about her.

keyTerms.meaning: She lies before him, waiting for יבום
The sister of the woman bound to him for יבום

phrases.english: If we say it is the sister of one under a prohibition of מצוה,
since by Torah law she is cast before him for yibum,
he encounters the sister of the woman bound to him!
phrases.notes: That case was already taught, so the משנה wouldn't be teaching it again here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'her sister' is the sister of an איסור מצוה woman.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By Torah law that woman is truly bound to him, so her sister is the 'sister of his זקוקה,' a case that is already taught and has other rules.

steps.title: It means the sister of an ערוה
steps.stepSummary: So the משנה is talking about the sister of a woman who is an ערוה to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the sister of a woman under an ערוה prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the משנה means the sister of an ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערוה is never bound to the יבם at all, so her sister is not the 'sister of his זקוקה.' That is why the sister may freely do חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Her sister who is her יבמה' means the sister of an ערוה. An ערוה is never bound to him, so her sister may do יבום.

phrases.english: Rather, it is the sister of one forbidden by a prohibition of ערוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining reading after step 19 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sister in the משנה is the sister of an ערוה.

steps.title: Why call rabbinic שניות an 'איסור מצוה'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said איסור מצוה means שניות. The גמרא asks why a rabbinic prohibition is called a 'מצוה' prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says an איסור מצוה means the שניות. Why is it called an 'איסור מצוה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's definition from step 13 and asks about the name. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שניות are only forbidden by the חכמים, not by a פסוק. So it seems strange to call them a prohibition 'of מצוה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary relatives, forbidden only by the חכמים

phrases.english: 'A prohibition of מצוה: these are the secondary relatives.'
Why is it called a prohibition of מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's definitions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a rabbinic prohibition is called an איסור מצוה.

steps.title: אביי: it is a מצוה to listen to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that it is called a מצוה prohibition because obeying the חכמים is itself a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question about the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition itself comes from the חכמים, but keeping it fulfills the general מצוה of obeying them. That is where the name 'איסור מצוה' comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The words, or rulings, of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: An 'איסור מצוה' is a rabbinic prohibition, the שניות. It gets the name 'מצוה' because there is a מצוה to obey the חכמים.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a מצוה to listen to the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִצְוָה לִשְׁמוֹעַ דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name comes from the מצוה to obey the חכמים.

steps.title: The משנה defines a prohibition of sanctity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: איסור קדושה refers to an אלמנה to a כהן גדול, or a גרושה or חלוצה to a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A prohibition of sanctity means a widow to a High Priest, or a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, which defines the term איסור קדושה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא explained איסור מצוה as the rabbinic שניות. Now it moves to the second label in the משנה. Here איסור קדושה covers the Torah prohibitions on whom a כהן may marry.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that comes from holiness
A widow, who is forbidden to a High Priest
A woman released from יבום through חליצה
A regular priest, not the High Priest

phrases.english: A prohibition of sanctity
is a widow to a High Priest,
or a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's term איסור מצוה to its second term, איסור קדושה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה, איסור קדושה means the Torah marriage prohibitions of כהנים.

steps.title: Why call it a prohibition of sanctity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the כהן prohibitions are called איסור קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why are they called a prohibition of sanctity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the name איסור קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a source that connects the כהן marriage prohibitions to holiness. It is a request for an explanation, not an attack.

phrases.english: And why are they called a prohibition of sanctity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the label quoted in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for calling the כהן prohibitions 'קדושה'.

steps.title: Because the Torah calls priests holy
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'קדושים יהיו לאלהיהם' is said about כהנים, right next to the marriage prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'They shall be holy to their God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that calls the כהנים holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that calls כהנים holy appears in the same section as the women they may not marry. So these prohibitions are tied to the כהן's holiness.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'They shall be holy to their God.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name comes from the פסוק calling כהנים holy, in the section about whom they may marry.

steps.title: רבי יהודה switches the labels
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי יהודה reverses the names: the כהן prohibitions are איסור מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה switches. A prohibition of מצוה is a widow to a High Priest, or a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה swaps the two labels of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules themselves do not change, only the names do. For רבי יהודה, the Torah prohibitions of כהנים are called איסור מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not argue about the הלכה. He only swaps which group is called by which name.

phrases.english: It was taught: רבי יהודה switches:
A prohibition of מצוה
is a widow to a High Priest,
or a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a reversed naming system for the same two groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהודה, the כהן prohibitions are איסור מצוה.

steps.title: Why call it a prohibition of מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, for רבי יהודה, the כהן prohibitions are called איסור מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called a prohibition of מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's reason for the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Torah prohibition is a מצוה, so the גמרא wants to know what makes these ones fit that name specifically.

phrases.english: And why is it called a prohibition of מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's label.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for calling the כהן prohibitions 'מצוה'.

steps.title: Because the Torah calls them מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אלה המצות' is the source of the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'These are the מצוות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the פסוק 'אלה המצות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק closes ספר ויקרא and sums up its laws as 'מצוות'. Since the כהן prohibitions are written in ויקרא, רבי יהודה calls them איסור מצוה.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'These are the מצוות.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:34, the last פסוק of the ספר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name comes from 'אלה המצות', which sums up the laws of ויקרא.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, rabbinic relatives are 'sanctity'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה calls the rabbinic שניות איסור קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A prohibition of sanctity means the secondary relatives forbidden by the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the other half of רבי יהודה's switch. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה used 'מצוה' for the כהן prohibitions, he uses 'קדושה' for the rabbinic שניות. This is the reverse of the משנה.

phrases.english: A prohibition of sanctity
is the secondary relatives, from rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהודה's swap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהודה, the rabbinic שניות are איסור קדושה.

steps.title: Why call a rabbinic rule 'sanctity'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a rabbinic prohibition is called איסור קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called a prohibition of sanctity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה would call a rabbinic rule 'holiness'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the כהנים, there is no פסוק for the שניות. So the גמרא needs a different kind of reason for the name.

phrases.english: And why is it called a prohibition of sanctity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 29's label.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why rabbinic שניות are described as קדושה.

steps.title: אביי: keeping the Sages' words makes one holy
steps.stepSummary: אביי says anyone who keeps the words of the חכמים is called holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Whoever keeps the words of the Sages is called holy.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a reason: listening to the חכמים earns the title 'holy'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches אביי's earlier answer about the word 'מצוה' in Step 22. Obeying rabbinic law is itself a mark of holiness, so the שניות can be called קדושה.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Whoever keeps the words of the Sages
is called holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כׇּל הַמְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים נִקְרָא קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Keeping rabbinic law makes a person holy, so it is called קדושה.

steps.title: רבא: then the one who disobeys is not wicked?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that אביי's wording suggests someone who ignores the חכמים is simply 'not holy', not wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: And whoever does not keep the words of the Sages, he is just not called holy, but he is not called wicked either?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's explanation by showing what it implies about someone who disobeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Holy' sounds like extra credit. If keeping rabbinic law only earns extra credit, then breaking it would only mean missing that credit. But someone who breaks the words of the חכמים is called a רשע, so אביי's wording is too weak.

phrases.english: רבא said to him:
And whoever does not keep the words of the Sages,
is it only that he is not called holy,
but he is not called wicked either?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that keeping rabbinic law earns the title 'holy'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That wording makes rabbinic law sound optional, as if disobeying only loses a bonus. But one who disobeys is a רשע.

steps.title: רבא: sanctify yourself with what is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that קדושה means holding yourself back even from what the Torah permits, which is what the שניות do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Sanctify yourself with what is permitted to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reason for the name איסור קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שניות are permitted by Torah law, but the חכמים told us to stay away from them. Holding back from something the Torah allows is what 'sanctify yourself' means. So the name describes the kind of prohibition, not a reward for keeping it.

keyTerms.meaning: With what is permitted to you

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, the שניות are called קדושה because of רבא's principle: sanctify yourself by holding back from what the Torah permits.
steps.whyThisMatters: קדש עצמך במותר לך is a famous principle, and here it is used to explain the basic idea behind rabbinic fences.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
Sanctify yourself with what is permitted to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: קַדֵּשׁ עַצְמְךָ בַּמּוּתָּר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדושה was a title given to someone who obeys the חכמים (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: קדושה means separating from what is Torah-permitted; the שניות are exactly that.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rabbinic שניות are 'קדושה' because they keep us from what the Torah permits.

steps.title: אלמנה to a כהן גדול: from נשואין or אירוסין alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'אלמנה לכהן גדול' and notes it is stated without limits, so it applies to a widow from נשואין or from אירוסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A widow to a High Priest': it is taught without any distinction, whether she was widowed from full marriage or from betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול and points out that the rule is general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say what kind of widow she is. So the גמרא learns that even a woman widowed after only אירוסין counts as an אלמנה forbidden to a כהן גדול, and she gets the same יבום rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches flatly, without making distinctions
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: 'A widow to a High Priest.'
It teaches this without distinction,
no difference whether from full marriage
or from betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of names and goes back to explain the scope of a case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's אלמנה to a כהן גדול includes a widow from אירוסין as well as from נשואין.

steps.title: Why can't ייבום override the prohibition for a widow from betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that a widow from נשואין cannot have ייבום with a כהן גדול. But it challenges the case of a widow from אירוסין, who is forbidden only by a single לא תעשה, which a עשה should normally override.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a widow from marriage: there is a positive command and a prohibition, and a positive command does not push aside a prohibition plus a positive command. But a widow from betrothal is just a prohibition alone. Let the positive command of ייבום come and push aside the prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the ruling from step 34 that even a widow from אירוסין gets only חליצה. It asks why the מצוה of ייבום does not override her single prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow from נשואין is no longer a בתולה, so a כהן גדול marrying her breaks the עשה of marrying a בתולה and the לאו against marrying a widow, and a עשה cannot override both together. A widow from אירוסין is still a בתולה, so only the לאו applies. The normal rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה says ייבום should win.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (the first case is fine, but...)
A positive command overrides a prohibition
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: The widow from אירוסין is still a בתולה, so the עשה of marrying a בתולה is not broken in her case. That is the whole reason she seems different.

phrases.english: Granted, a widow from marriage —
is a positive command and a prohibition,
phrases.notes: The positive command is that a כהן גדול marries a בתולה (ויקרא 21:13); the prohibition is against marrying a widow (ויקרא 21:14).

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה.
phrases.english: and a positive command does not override a prohibition plus a positive command.
But a widow from betrothal —
it is only a prohibition,
let the positive command come and override the prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope set in step 34, which includes a widow from אירוסין
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a widow from אירוסין gets only חליצה with a כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single לאו should be pushed aside by the עשה of ייבום, using the general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה

steps.title: The extra word ״יבמתו״ teaches that women forbidden by a לאו get only חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב learns from the extra word ״יבמתו״ that there is a יבמה who goes to חליצה but not to ייבום. These are women forbidden to the יבם by a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: the verse says 'his יבמה shall go up to the gate.' The word 'his יבמה' was not needed, so why does the verse say it? To teach that there is one kind of יבמה who goes up for חליצה but not for ייבום. Which one is she? Women forbidden by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל answers the challenge with a פסוק. An extra word shows that in a case of a לאו, ייבום does not override; the woman does חליצה instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have said 'and she shall go up to the gate' without ״יבמתו״. The extra word points to a woman who is still called his יבמה for חליצה but cannot have ייבום. That is חייבי לאוין, which includes a widow from אירוסין who falls to a כהן גדול. So here the Torah itself sets aside the usual rule of עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse did not need to say this word
The ceremony that releases the יבמה without marriage
Women forbidden by a regular prohibition, a לאו

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule for the whole topic. Women forbidden by a לאו do חליצה and not ייבום.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
The verse says: "His yevama shall go up to the gate,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: since the verse did not need to say "his yevama,"
why does the verse say "his yevama"?
To teach that there is one kind of yevama
who goes up for chalitza but does not go up for yibum,
and which is she? Those forbidden by a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35 with a פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source showing ייבום does not override a לאו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a עשה normally overrides a single לאו, ייבום should be allowed for a widow from אירוסין
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word ״יבמתו״ shows that חייבי לאוין do חליצה and not ייבום

steps.title: Maybe the extra word means women forbidden by כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״יבמתו״ should mean חייבי לאוין. Maybe it means women forbidden under penalty of כרת, who would then do חליצה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means women forbidden by כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's reading. Maybe the extra word refers to a different group: חייבי כריתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says there is a יבמה who gets חליצה without ייבום. It does not say which group she belongs to. Women forbidden by כרת also cannot have ייבום, so the word could just as well be pointing at them.

keyTerms.meaning: Women forbidden under penalty of כרת, a more severe prohibition

phrases.english: But say it means those forbidden by karet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which group step 36's derivation refers to
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״יבמתו״ refers to חייבי לאוין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could equally refer to חייבי כריתות, who also cannot have ייבום

steps.title: Only a woman who could have ייבום can have חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'if the man does not want to take her' shows that חליצה happens only where ייבום was an option. Women forbidden by כרת can never have ייבום, so they get no חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And if the man does not want to take her.' This means that if he does want, he does ייבום. So anyone who can go up for ייבום can go up for חליצה, and anyone who cannot go up for ייבום cannot go up for חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״יבמתו״ cannot mean חייבי כריתות. A different פסוק links חליצה to the possibility of ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'if he does not want' implies he had the choice to want her. So חליצה only applies where ייבום could have happened. With כרת, ייבום never applies at all, and the bond between them never even starts, so there is no חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם לֹא יַחְפּוֹץ הָאִישׁ לָקַחַת״,
phrases.english: The verse says: "And if the man does not want to take,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: which implies that if he wants, he does yibum.
Whoever can go up for yibum can go up for chalitza,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין עוֹלֶה לְיִיבּוּם — אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לַחֲלִיצָה.
phrases.english: and whoever cannot go up for yibum cannot go up for chalitza.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם לֹא יַחְפּוֹץ הָאִישׁ לָקַחַת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second פסוק sets a general rule linking חליצה to ייבום
steps.terutzMaskana: חייבי כריתות can never have ייבום, so they get no חליצה, and ״יבמתו״ cannot refer to them

steps.title: Then women forbidden by a לאו should also get no חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. By the same rule, חייבי לאוין cannot have ייבום, so they should get no חליצה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then those forbidden by a prohibition too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns step 38's rule against רב's answer. Women forbidden by a לאו also cannot have ייבום, so the rule would take away their חליצה as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 said that no possible ייבום means no חליצה. חייבי לאוין cannot have ייבום, as step 36 said. So the rule seems to remove חליצה for them too, which would leave the word ״יבמתו״ with nothing to refer to.

phrases.english: If so, those forbidden by a prohibition too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 38's rule against the conclusion of step 36
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חייבי לאוין get חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By step 38's rule, a woman who cannot have ייבום gets no חליצה, and חייבי לאוין cannot have ייבום

steps.title: The Torah included one group through ״יבמתו״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah specially included one group in חליצה through the word ״יבמתו״, even though that group cannot have ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Torah included them with the word 'his יבמה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra word ״יבמתו״ makes an exception to the general rule of step 38 for one group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38's rule is the general rule, but ״יבמתו״ makes an exception for one kind of woman who does חליצה without ייבום. So one group stays included and the other is left out. This leads straight into the next question: which group?

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah included (literally: the Merciful One included)

phrases.english: But the Torah included through "his yevama."
phrases.notes: The word רַבִּי here is a verb meaning 'included', not the title רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 39 by going back to the derivation of step 36
steps.terutzResolutionType: A special inclusion from the פסוק overrides the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No ייבום means no חליצה for every group
steps.terutzMaskana: ״יבמתו״ keeps one group in חליצה even without ייבום

steps.title: What made you choose לאוין over כריתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the choice. Why should the included group be חייבי לאוין and the excluded group be חייבי כריתות, and not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to choose this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what reason there is to say ״יבמתו״ includes חייבי לאוין while the general rule leaves out חייבי כריתות. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two פסוקים: one includes a group, and one excludes. Both groups cannot have ייבום, so the גמרא wants a reason for matching the inclusion to לאוין and the exclusion to כריתות.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? A request for the reason behind a choice

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what reason do you have to say the included group is לאוין and not כריתות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way step 40 and step 38 split the two groups
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ״יבמתו״ includes חייבי לאוין rather than חייבי כריתות
